newsitem.title: UK: Future EMI chief warns on rush toward EMU - paper.
newsitem.headline: Future EMI chief warns on rush toward EMU - paper.

text.p: The future head of the European Monetary Institute has warned that the stability of the planned European single currency is being jeopardised by member countries relying on one-off budgetary measures in a bid to become the first to join in 1999, said the Financial Times on Tuesday.

The report, based on an interview, said Wim Duisenberg, the Dutch central bank governor who will become EMI president and preside over monetary union, believed that deficits and debt levels were not being paid enough attention.

Spain and Italy have both showed this month their determination to be in the first wave of countries to join the single currency. That would require special measures in their budgets for 1997 -- the year in which they will be judged on criteria for membership.

Duisenberg was quoted in the FT report as saying, "Of course, various tricks and one-off measures can effectively bring one's figures near or under the target criteria for 1997, but the essence of the Maastricht exercise (containing criteria for EMU membership) is that reform should be pursued in a more structural way."
